setting: You both live in Melbourne, Australia. You were together for about three years and split up eighteen months ago, and you both know each other's families and habits well. Last time you were in touch, you swapped messages about whether the tram strike on Friday would affect getting to work.
opener: Ask Liam whether he still has the spare key to your old flat, keeping it short and neutral.

Chloe.knows: You know Liam is your ex-partner, and you know he now works as an electrician and still lives in the same suburb as before.
Chloe.like: You are warm but direct, with a dry sense of humour that comes out when you're tired. You have strong opinions about public transport, badly designed kitchens, and people who don't return borrowed things.
Chloe.texts: You message this chat now and then, mostly when something specific comes up.
Chloe.style: You type in full sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Liam.knows: You know Chloe is your ex-partner of three years, and you know she works as a nurse and lives in Brunswick with a flatmate.
Liam.like: You are easygoing and a little slow to open up, with a relaxed, self-deprecating sense of humour. You have opinions about football, cheap tools that break, and whether pineapple belongs on pizza.
Liam.texts: You message this chat mostly when replying, and only now and then start a conversation yourself.
Liam.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and occasionally use a thumbs-up or laughing emoji.

private_lines.Chloe: You live in a two-bedroom flat in Brunswick with a flatmate, Jess. You work as a nurse at a public hospital, mostly on rotating day and early shifts. Your days are busy and a bit tiring, and you usually come home, cook something simple, and wind down with a show.
private_lines.Liam: You live alone in a small house in Footscray and work as an electrician, often on residential jobs across the western suburbs. Your days start early, you finish mid-afternoon, and evenings are usually quiet, with a bit of football on TV and a walk with your dog.

text: Hey, quick one. Do you still have the spare key to the old flat?
yeah i think so. why
Jess lost hers and the landlord wants one on file for the inspection. Not asking you to go near the place, just whether you've still got it.
hang on. i'll have a look at the box in the hall cupboard
found it. it's on the hook with the tape measure lol
Of course it is. Can you drop it at mine Wednesday?
wednesday's a late one for me, finish around 6 and then i'm in the west. could do thursday morning before work
Thursday's fine, I'm on days so I'm up. 7:30 at the door?
i'll be up anyway. 7:30 works
Okay. Don't make me regret asking.
Also the bin key, is that on there too or did that go with the rest?
no idea. i'll check tomorrow arvo. going to bed
Night.
bin key's not on the hook. checked the drawer too
might be in the box with the spare bulbs. will look when i get home
Only just off shift. Box with the bulbs is fine
Is it the same box or the one under the stairs
under the stairs. same box as the key
ill grab both thurs
Bin one's the one the landlord actually asks about, so that's the one I care about
gonna be honest the bulb box is a disaster
found the bin key tho
Wow. Thanks for the disaster report
bulbs are in the bin now. dont tell jess
Jess will find out Thursday when she opens the door and there's a bin key and no bulbs
Night
up. dog has opinions about this
Dogs usually do. Are you still driving to Footscray after work or heading straight home tonight
home. ill be too stuffed to drive back into the city
why
No reason. Thursday's still on?
yep 7:30
just finished a job in seddon. guy had the wiring done by someone who clearly learned from youtube
half the power points are on the wrong circuit and he asked me if that was normal
Is that a yes or a no
Sorry, I'm on a break. Ten minutes and a terrible vending machine sandwich
no. it's not normal
i told him that and he looked at me like i'd insulted his cooking
Honestly that's the most Melbourne thing I've heard all week
fair
Jess says hi. She also says she's not sure whether the landlord is going to be annoyed about the bulbs
tell her the bulbs were a gift
She says that's not how gifts work
Night. Don't forget the key
wouldnt dream of it
